interpretation.title: CRM Cloud Migration Plan
interpretation.audience: Chief Technology Officer (CTO) and senior leadership
interpretation.objective: Present a detailed, realistic migration strategy that moves the current CRM to the cloud within 6 weeks, adheres to a tight budget, and ensures zero downtime for end‑users.
missing_info: Current on‑premises CRM platform and version
Target cloud provider or preferred cloud environment
Specific budget amount allocated for the migration
Total data volume and any large attachments/files
Compliance or regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA)
Available internal resources and skill sets (e.g., DBAs, network engineers)
Existing integration points with other systems
conflicts: Tight budget versus aggressive 6‑week timeline with zero‑downtime requirement
assumptions: User count to be confirmed by requester; assume 150‑250 active users for sizing purposes
Current CRM is an on‑premises solution (e.g., Microsoft Dynamics or custom app) that can be replicated in the cloud
Target cloud provider not yet selected; plan remains provider‑agnostic and outlines options for major providers (AWS, Azure, GCP)
Budget is limited but sufficient to cover licensing, migration tools, and minimal consulting; assume $75,000‑$100,000 available
Data volume is moderate (under 5 TB) and can be transferred using standard bandwidth and incremental sync techniques
No extraordinary compliance constraints beyond typical data protection; assume standard GDPR‑compliant controls are required
Internal team includes at least one senior DBA, one network engineer, and a project manager; external expertise can be engaged as needed
Existing integrations will be catalogued and re‑implemented post‑migration; assume they can be handled within the project scope

key_decisions: Phase 1 (Weeks 1‑2): Discovery & Planning – led by Project Manager and Business Analyst; confirm user count, current CRM details, data volume, and integration inventory.
Phase 2 (Weeks 3‑4): Architecture & Pilot Migration – Solution Architect and Cloud Engineer design provider‑agnostic architecture and execute a zero‑downtime pilot for a subset of users.
Phase 3 (Weeks 5‑6): Full Cut‑over & Validation – DevOps Engineer and QA Engineer perform incremental sync, final cut‑over, and post‑migration validation ensuring zero downtime.
Budget range assumed: $75,000‑$100,000 covering licensing, migration tools, and limited consulting.
Zero‑downtime is achieved via dual‑write (shadow) replication and cut‑over during low‑usage window.
User count assumed 150‑250 active users for sizing; actual count to be confirmed in Phase 1.
Primary cloud provider remains agnostic; options for AWS, Azure, and GCP are outlined with comparable cost estimates.

plan.description: Write an executive summary that captures the objective, timeline, budget range, zero‑downtime guarantee, and key assumptions for quick CTO review.
plan.instructions: Summarize the migration goal, 6‑week schedule, $75‑$100k budget, zero‑downtime approach, and the main assumptions (user count, cloud‑agnostic, data volume).

plan.description: Draft the project scope defining what is in‑scope and out‑of‑scope, deliverables, and success criteria.
plan.instructions: List in‑scope items (CRM data, configurations, integrations, user access), out‑of‑scope items (major custom code rewrites), deliverables (migration plan, test results, cut‑over checklist), and success criteria (zero downtime, performance parity, user acceptance).

plan.description: Create a detailed timeline table showing weeks, activities, owners, and milestones.
plan.instructions: Table columns: Week, Activity, Owner(s), Milestone/Deliverable. Populate according to the three phases defined in key decisions.

plan.description: Estimate effort per role, apply company rate card, and compute total cost.
plan.instructions: Estimate person‑days for each role (Project Manager, Business Analyst, Solution Architect, Cloud Engineer, DevOps Engineer, QA Engineer, Security Specialist). Use standard rates to produce total cost and show it falls within the $75‑$100k range.

plan.description: Outline the migration approach, tools, and zero‑downtime technique.
plan.instructions: Describe provider‑agnostic architecture options, data replication method (dual‑write/CDC), pilot migration steps, cut‑over strategy, and validation procedures.

plan.description: Identify risks, mitigation actions, and contingency plans.
plan.instructions: List key risks (budget overrun, timeline slip, data sync issues, compliance gaps), assign owners, and provide mitigation/contingency steps.

plan.description: Document all assumptions, open questions, and any conflicts to be resolved.
plan.instructions: List the assumptions from the analysis, the missing information items, and note the budget‑timeline conflict with the mitigation approach.

issues_found.problem: The risk management content is malformed and contains stray tokens (e.g., "type", ":", "bullets", "items") making it unreadable and incomplete.
issues_found.fix_instruction: Rewrite the Risk Management section as a clean, bullet‑point list. For each risk include: Risk description, Owner (matching roles used elsewhere), Mitigation strategy, and Contingency plan. Ensure the formatting is consistent with the rest of the document and that all three key risks (budget overrun, timeline slip, data sync issues, compliance gaps) are clearly presented.
